svg.title: Choosing how to connect to an EC2 instance
svg.desc: Four questions in order. Does the instance boot, with a working network? If not, use the EC2 Serial Console. Does it run SSM Agent with an instance profile and a route to Systems Manager? If yes, use Session Manager. Is a public IP with port 22 reachable from you? If not, use an EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint. Otherwise use EC2 Instance Connect over the public IP, and classic SSH with a long-lived key pair when the instance cannot run the EC2 Instance Connect package. Tools such as scp, rsync and Ansible work with your own key over EC2 Instance Connect, an endpoint tunnel or SSH over Session Manager.
svg.text: Choosing how to connect to an EC2 instance
Ask the questions in order; the first answer that fits wins
1. Does it boot, with a working network?
broken sshd_config, bad network setup, boot failure
2. SSM Agent and an instance profile?
and a route to Systems Manager (NAT or VPC endpoints)
3. Public IP with port 22 reachable?
from you, or from the Instance Connect prefix list
EC2 Instance Connect (direct)
IAM pushes a 60-second key, no keys to share
yes
no
yes
EC2 Serial Console
Nitro, account setting, password user; last resort
Session Manager
no open port, IAM only, sessions logged
EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint
private IP is enough, no bastion, no agent
Classic SSH with a key pair
legacy tooling; long-lived keys to rotate
no
yes
no
no package
scp, rsync or Ansible: use SSH with your own key over EC2 Instance Connect, an endpoint tunnel or SSH over Session Manager.
VPN, Direct Connect and bastion hosts only change the network path; one of these methods still opens the shell.
